questions.explanation: The image is a histological section of epidermis. The marked layers correspond to stratum corneum, stratum granulosum, stratum spinosum, and stratum basale; therefore option D gives the correct mapping. Thin hairy skin has these four layers. Thick glabrous skin of palms and soles additionally has a clear stratum lucidum between stratum corneum and stratum granulosum.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of epidermis is referred to as the prickle cell layer?
questions.explanation: Stratum spinosum is the prickle-cell layer. Its keratinocytes are attached by desmosomes. During H&E preparation the cells shrink away from one another except at these attachments, making the desmosomes appear as spines or prickles.

questions.question: In which of the following layers of the epidermis are multiple layers of intertwining anucleate keratinocytes seen?
questions.explanation: Stratum corneum is composed of multiple layers of flattened, anucleate, keratinized cells that can intertwine. Keratinocytes originate in the stratum basale and progressively lose their nuclei and dehydrate as they migrate superficially. The thick stratum corneum contributes to the epidermal barrier against microbes and fluid loss.

questions.explanation: The marked region points to intercellular adhesions formed by desmosomes. Hemidesmosomes instead mediate cell-to-extracellular-matrix adhesion.

questions.explanation: Arrector pili are smooth muscles. They connect the undersurface of hair follicles to papillary dermis and are sympathetically innervated. Their contraction produces hair erection and goose flesh and helps squeeze sebaceous secretion into the follicle. The source notes their absence in several specialized hair regions.

structuredExplanation.source_transcription_ocr:
Arrector pili muscles are smooth muscles.


They connect the undersurface of the hair follicles to the papillary dermis and are supplied by
sympathetic nerves. Contraction of these muscles leads to the erection of hair, tiny bumps on the
skin and thus produces a ‘goose flesh’ appearance. The other effect of the contraction of arrector
pili is the squeezing out of the secretions of the sebaceous glands into the hair follicle. They are
absent in facial, axillary and pubic hairs, eyelashes, eyebrows and hairs around the nostrils and
external auditory meatus.

structuredExplanation.source_transcription_ocr:
The structures marked X and Y are the endothelium and Bowman's membrane, respectively.

The human cornea has five layers, From the anterior to posterior, the layers of the human cornea
are as follows:

+ Corneal epithelium - It is the outermost layer made up of non-keratinized stratified squamous
epithelium, It is continuous with the conjunctival epithelium.

+ Bowman's layer - The anterior-limiting lamina lies behind the corneal epithelium. It contains a
dense mass of collagen (mainly type I collagen fibrils) set in a matrix similar to that of the


substantia propria.
+ Corneal stroma (also substantia propria) - It is a thick, transparent middle layer, consisting of
regularly arranged collagen fibers along with sparsely distributed interconnected keratocytes.

+ Descemet's membrane - It is a thin acellular layer that serves as the modified basement

membrane of the corneal endothelium, from which the cells are derived. This layer is composed
mainly of collagen type IV fibrils.

+ Corneal endothelium - The endothelium covers the posterior surface of the cornea and consists,
of a single layer of squamous cells.

The sixth layer called Dua’s layer or pre-Descemet's layer has been recently discovered, located
between the stroma and the Descemet's membrane. ‘

questions.question: Arrange from outer to inner the layers of the retina given below: A-Retinal pigment epithelium; B-Inner plexiform layer; C-Nerve fiber layer; D-Inner nuclear layer; E-External limiting membrane.
questions.explanation: From outer to inner, the listed retinal layers are retinal pigment epithelium (A), external limiting membrane (E), inner nuclear layer (D), inner plexiform layer (B), and nerve fiber layer (C). Hence A-E-D-B-C is correct.

questions.question: Identify the structure shown in the histological image below.
questions.explanation: The histological image is the cochlea, identified by the organ of Corti. The cochlea makes about 2.75 turns around the modiolus. The vestibular and basilar membranes divide the bony labyrinth into scala vestibuli (perilymph), scala media (endolymph) and scala tympani (perilymph).

structuredExplanation.source_transcription_ocr:
The above histological image is that of the cochlea which can be identified by the presence of
characteristic organ of Corti.


The cochlea consists of a bony canal that makes 2.75 spiral turns around an axis of bone known as
the modiolus. A shelf of bone from the modiolus forms a ridge known as the spiral lamina.

The basilar membrane supporting the organ of Corti extends from the spiral lamina to the outer
wall of the cochlea. The vestibular membrane runs from the spiral lamina to the outer wall above
the basilar membrane. These two membranes divide the bony labyrinth into three cavities:

+ Scala vestibule - located between the roof of the labyrinth and the vestibular membrane, is lined
by mesenchymal cells and contains perilymph.

+ Scala media - located between the vestibular membrane and basilar membrane, contains
endolymph.

+ Scala tympani - located between the basilar membrane and the floor of the labyrinth, is lined by
mesenchymal cells and contains perilymph. \S

questions.question: The gelatinous component of the crista ampullaris that extends from the crista to the roof of the ampulla is known as:
questions.explanation: The gelatinous component over the crista ampullaris is the cupula. Hair-cell stereocilia and kinocilium project into the cupula. During head rotation, lag of endolymph deflects the cupula and stimulates the hair cells, contributing to spatial orientation.

structuredExplanation.source_transcription_ocr:
The gelatinous component of the crista ampullaris that extends from the crista to the roof of the
ampullae is known as the cupula.

The ampullary cupula, or cupula, provides a sense of spatial orientation. It is located in each of
the ampullae of the three semicircular canals. In the crista ampullaris, hair cells that have several
stereocilia associated with each kinocilium, are embedded into the gelatinous matrix of the cupula
ina specific pattern that is functionally significant. The lag of endolymph on the rotational
movement of the head deflects the cupula and hence stimulates the hair cells.
